# ScottSearch 0.1.6 — persistent, changed-files-only startup

This human-testing release replaces the remaining full-vault work on normal
startup. ScottSearch now restores a local lexical snapshot and reconciles it
against inexpensive file fingerprints, so unchanged note bodies are not read
or tokenized again after the initial 0.1.6 build.

## Changed

- The first 0.1.6 run builds a versioned lexical snapshot in ScottSearch's
  local vault plugin folder.
- Later launches compare path, modification time, and size, then read only new
  or changed notes and remove deleted or newly ignored entries.
- The snapshot persists compressed metadata and derived term counts rather
  than a second copy of note bodies.
- Exact-phrase searches lazily read only plausible phrase candidates for final
  verification. Result previews lazily read the small displayed result set.
- Small edits append compact journal records instead of rewriting the whole
  snapshot. After the index is idle, the journal is compressed into a fresh
  snapshot.
- Existing semantic vectors remain reusable. ScottSearch reads note content
  for semantics only when an embedding is missing, stale, or belongs to a
  different provider.
- A corrupt snapshot, incompatible schema, or index-affecting settings change
  safely falls back to the bounded four-note rebuild introduced in 0.1.5.
- The manual **Rebuild index** control still performs a deliberate full rebuild
  and replaces the snapshot.

## Verification

Automated coverage proves that a warm startup with identical fingerprints
schedules zero unchanged note reads, while changed, new, deleted, corrupt,
settings-mismatched, exact-phrase, incremental-journal, and semantic-cache
cases remain correct. The synthetic 1,000-note storage test also verifies that
the compressed derived snapshot is smaller than the source text it represents
and contains no note-body field.

Real Obsidian startup timing remains part of the public human beta. Please run
one initial build and then a second warm start, reporting approximate timing
without publishing note text, private paths, or credentials.

## Privacy and compatibility

The lexical snapshot stays in ScottSearch's local plugin directory. It contains
titles, paths, tags, file fingerprints, and derived term counts, which may still
be sensitive metadata, but no full note-body copy. It is never uploaded.
Uninstalling ScottSearch removes the plugin and its cache; a manual rebuild
replaces it. Optional Ollama behavior is unchanged, and unreleased on-device
experiments remain excluded from the public bundle.

ScottSearch supports Obsidian 1.7.2 or later on macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone,
iPad, and Android. This remains a pre-release for human testing rather than a
stable Community-directory submission.

## Install or update

BRAT users can update ScottSearch normally. For a manual installation,
download `scottsearch-0.1.6.zip` below, unzip it, place the enclosed
`scottsearch` folder inside `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/`, restart Obsidian, and
enable ScottSearch under **Settings → Community plugins**.

Please submit sanitized cold-versus-warm results through the
[friendly beta form](https://github.com/c4g-john/scottsearch-for-obsidian/issues/new?template=beta_test_report.yml).
Do not include private note text, paths, or credentials in public reports.

To roll back, reinstall 0.1.5 from its release page. Neither update nor rollback
deletes notes. Version 0.1.5 remains available as superseded release history.
